variants.subject: Before we say anything else, here's who we are
variants.body:
{{RANDOM | A quick introduction | Just wanted to introduce ourselves | We wanted to reach out first}}.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

DabbahWala is a home-style Indian food delivery service based in Michigan.

We don't run a restaurant. We don't have a dine-in space.
We cook from a kitchen, to order, and deliver the same day.

The food is meant to feel like something cooked at home — lighter oils, fresh vegetables, no MSG, no artificial enhancers. Meals made in small batches, not in bulk.

We built DabbahWala for people who want to eat well on regular days, not just special ones.

Over the next few emails, we'll share a little more about how it works and what we cook.
No pressure to do anything with it.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: DabbahWala — what we are and what we're not
variants.body:
It's easier to start with what we're not.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

We're not a restaurant. We're not a meal-prep service. We're not a catering company.

DabbahWala is a home-style Indian food kitchen that cooks and delivers fresh meals daily, directly to your door.

We cook only after orders come in. That means nothing sits in a warmer waiting for you. Food is made fresh and delivered the same day.

The cooking is intentional — lighter oils, fresh vegetables, no MSG, small batches. Food that feels easy to eat on a regular Tuesday, not just a special occasion.

That's what we're building toward. We'll explain more over the next few notes.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: Why home-style cooking is actually different
variants.body:
It's not just a marketing phrase.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

{{RANDOM | When people hear "home-style," they often assume it means simple or basic | "Home-style" gets used loosely — we want to explain what it actually means to us | The phrase "home-style" gets thrown around a lot, so let us be specific}}.

At DabbahWala, it means cooking the way most households actually cook:

Lighter oils that don't leave you feeling heavy.
No MSG or artificial flavor boosters.
Vegetables that are cut and prepared the day of cooking, not days before.
Spices used in balance — not to overpower, but to make the food genuinely enjoyable over time.

Restaurant food is designed to impress once. Home-style food is designed to be good every day.

That's the difference. And it matters when you're eating from the same kitchen week after week.

We'll share more about our menu and how we keep it from feeling repetitive next.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: The difference between restaurant food and what we make
variants.body:
It comes down to who the food is made for.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

Restaurant food is made to impress. Rich, bold, indulgent.
That's appropriate — it's a special experience.

But it's not the kind of food you can eat every day without feeling it.

At DabbahWala, we cook the opposite way.

Meals are lighter. Oils are everyday cooking oils, not heavy restaurant bases. Vegetables are fresh, not pre-processed. Nothing is cooked in bulk and reheated.

{{RANDOM | The goal is food that feels good the second, third, and fourth time you eat it | We think about how food feels on an ordinary Thursday, not just a Friday night out | We build every dish around whether you'd want to eat it again in three days}}.

That's what home-style means to us — food that fits into real life, not just occasions.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: What "home-style" actually means in our kitchen
variants.body:
We use the phrase a lot. Here's what's behind it.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

Home-style cooking at DabbahWala isn't about presentation or novelty.
It's about how the food is actually made.

{{RANDOM | We cook with lighter, everyday oils | We avoid the heavy bases and rich oils most restaurant kitchens rely on | Cooking oil makes a bigger difference than most people realize — so we use lighter ones}}.
No MSG. No artificial flavor enhancers.
Vegetables are prepared the day of cooking, not days in advance.
We cook in small batches so nothing sits around.

The result is food that tastes clean and familiar — the way a good home-cooked meal feels after a long day.

Not trying to be fancy. Just trying to be the food you'd actually want to eat on a regular week.

– DabbahWala Kitchen Team

variants.subject: We cook your food after you order it. Here's why that matters.
variants.body:
It's a small detail that changes a lot.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

Most food delivery businesses cook in advance. Meals are prepared in the morning, loaded into containers, and dispatched throughout the day.

We do it differently.

At DabbahWala, meals are cooked only after orders come in. That means when your order arrives, it was made for you — not sitting in a warmer since 9am.

{{RANDOM | Fresh food tastes different. Not just marginally — noticeably | You can tell the difference between food cooked that morning and food cooked for you | It's the kind of freshness that makes you want to order again}}.

We also keep portion sizes honest and use fresh vegetables prepared the same day. No shortcuts with frozen or pre-cut produce.

It takes more effort. But it's the only way the food actually holds up over time.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: Fresh food, every single day
variants.body:
This isn't marketing — it's just how we operate.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

Here's how a typical day at DabbahWala works:

Orders come in → we cook → food is delivered the same day.

{{RANDOM | No pre-cooking. No holding trays. No reheating | Nothing sits in a container waiting for a delivery window | What you receive was cooked after you ordered it}}.

Vegetables are prepped fresh each morning. Spices are measured per batch, not poured from bulk containers. Everything is cooked in small quantities so quality doesn't slip.

We built DabbahWala this way because we believe fresh food is the foundation — and cutting corners there undermines everything else.

Next we'll share how our menu works and why it rotates.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: How we keep the food tasting like it was made today
variants.body:
Because it was.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

The reason DabbahWala food tastes fresh isn't luck. It's the process.

We cook only after orders are placed. That's the starting point. No pre-made meals waiting to be reheated.

Then:
Vegetables are cut and prepared the morning of delivery.
Meals are cooked in small batches — not industrial quantities.
Food leaves the kitchen and arrives the same day.

{{RANDOM | It's more work than cooking in bulk. But it's the only way to maintain what matters most: food that actually feels fresh when it arrives | We chose this approach over efficiency. Because efficiency at the cost of freshness defeats the whole purpose | The extra effort is worth it — it's the difference between food you eat and food you genuinely enjoy}}.

– DabbahWala Kitchen Team

variants.subject: You'll never eat the same thing twice
variants.body:
We built it that way on purpose.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

One of the quiet frustrations with food delivery is repetition.
Good food becomes average when it shows up the exact same way every week.

{{RANDOM | At DabbahWala, we rotate the menu regularly | Our menu changes frequently so eating well stays interesting | Dishes rotate so you're never stuck choosing between the same five options}}.

There are always a few options to choose from each day — different proteins, different preparations, seasonal vegetables.

We keep dishes light enough that you can eat them often, and varied enough that you actually want to.

{{RANDOM | The goal isn't variety for its own sake | We're not rotating menus just to seem interesting | Menu rotation isn't a gimmick}}. It's about making DabbahWala the kind of food you can genuinely eat three or four times a week without getting tired of it.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: Why our menu changes regularly
variants.body:
It wasn't an obvious decision. But it was the right one.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

Early on, we offered a fixed menu. Simple, consistent, easy to manage.

The problem: even people who loved the food started ordering less frequently over time.
Not because anything changed — but because repetition quietly kills appetite.

So we changed the model.

Now, dishes at DabbahWala rotate regularly. You'll see familiar comfort dishes alongside new preparations throughout the week.

{{RANDOM | Enough variety to keep things interesting. Enough familiarity to feel comforting | Not so different that it feels unfamiliar — just different enough that you're genuinely curious what's on today | The goal is food you want to order on a Monday as much as a Friday}}.

It's a simple change that made a real difference in how often people come back.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: More variety than you'd expect from a delivery kitchen
variants.body:
Here's what the menu actually looks like.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

On any given day at DabbahWala, you'll find a few options to choose from — different proteins, different preparations, sometimes a special based on what's fresh.

Dishes rotate regularly. So if you ordered dal and rice last week, something different is likely leading the menu this week.

{{RANDOM | We don't just make Indian food — we make the kind of Indian food that fits into everyday eating | The cooking is rooted in how people actually eat at home, not what looks good on a restaurant menu | Familiar flavors, thoughtfully prepared, and varied enough that ordering regularly doesn't get old}}.

If you ever want to see what's on the menu today, you can reply with Menu and we'll send it over.

Or check it out at https://www.dabbahwala.com whenever you're ready.

– DabbahWala Team

variants.subject: Ordering from DabbahWala is simpler than you think
variants.body:
We tried to strip out as many steps as possible.

Hi {{firstName|there}},

You can order from DabbahWala a few different ways:

1. Visit https://www.dabbahwala.com and order directly online.
2. Reply **Menu** to this email and we'll send you today's options and help you order personally.
3. Set up a subscription if you want meals without thinking about it every day.

{{RANDOM | Most people start with a single order to try us out. That's completely fine | No commitment required — you can order once and see if it's right for you | Ordering once to try it is always the easiest place to start}}.

Delivery is complimentary on orders over $35. Food is cooked fresh and arrives the same day.

If you have any questions before ordering, just reply to this email. We're usually quick to respond.

– DabbahWala Team
